just_in.title: HIV Prevention Funding Cuts Leave Immigrant Communities Without a Safety Net
just_in.excerpt: Federal grant terminations and proposed budget cuts totaling $1.5 billion threaten decades of progress against HIV, with Latino and immigrant populations bearing the heaviest burden as ICE enforcement drives patients away from clinics.
just_in.image_caption: Community health workers conduct preventive screenings at outreach events that serve as a lifeline for underserved populations. Federal funding cuts to the CDC threaten to dismantle this infrastructure nationwide.
just_in.nri_angle: HIV prevention funding cuts and immigration enforcement are creating compounding barriers for immigrant communities seeking healthcare, with Latino populations seeing a 50% drop in clinic visits and South Asian diaspora members facing loss of community health center services.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: UK's New PM Burnham Scraps VAT on Electricity Bills in First Policy Move
just_in.excerpt: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced the removal of value-added tax from domestic electricity bills starting October 1, saving households around £45 a year in his first major policy action.
just_in.image_caption: Andy Burnham at 10 Downing Street. The 56-year-old former Mayor of Greater Manchester became Britain's Prime Minister on Monday after Keir Starmer stepped down.
just_in.nri_angle: The UK is home to 1.8 million people of Indian origin, making it one of the largest NRI communities in the world. Rising energy costs have been a persistent concern for Indian families in Britain, particularly those running small businesses or supporting multi-generational households. The VAT cut will directly reduce their electricity bills from October.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: Bitcoin Climbs Past $65,500 as ETF Inflows and Clarity Act Progress Fuel Rally
just_in.excerpt: Five straight days of institutional inflows totaling over $600 million and a breakthrough on crypto legislation have pushed Bitcoin to its highest level in weeks, though India's punitive tax regime keeps diaspora investors on the sidelines.
just_in.image_caption: Bitcoin exchange-traded fund inflows have totaled more than $600 million over five consecutive sessions, reversing weeks of institutional selling. The cryptocurrency was trading near $65,500 on Tuesday, its highest level in two weeks.
just_in.nri_angle: India's 30% flat tax and 1% TDS on crypto, left unchanged in the 2026 budget, continue to push Indian diaspora investors toward offshore platforms even as Bitcoin rallies on ETF inflows and U.S. regulatory progress.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: From Rajma Rice to Puran Poli: How Strangers Fed Delhi's NEET Protesters
just_in.excerpt: Volunteers from across India brought home-cooked meals, snacks, and water to sustain student protesters at Jantar Mantar, turning a political sit-in into a display of grassroots solidarity through food.
just_in.image_caption: Volunteers prepare plates for a community meal. At Delhi's Jantar Mantar, strangers and volunteers have sustained NEET protesters with home-cooked meals, tea, and water for over six weeks.
just_in.nri_angle: For the Indian diaspora, the food solidarity at Jantar Mantar echoes the cultural tradition of community feeding during protests, from the langars of the farmers' movement to informal food networks at student agitations, offering a familiar emotional connection to the movement.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: Why Drying Potatoes Before Frying Is the Key to Preventing Oil Splatters
just_in.excerpt: Chef Ranveer Brar's go-to tip for safer, mess-free frying comes down to one overlooked step: removing surface moisture from cut potatoes before they hit the oil.
just_in.image_caption: Cut potato pieces being fried in a pan of hot oil. Drying potatoes thoroughly before frying reduces dangerous oil splatters caused by surface moisture reacting with hot oil.
just_in.nri_angle: Indian kitchens frequently rely on deep-frying in a kadai for staples like samosas, pakoras, and aloo tikki, making oil splatter prevention especially relevant for home cooks in the diaspora.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: Indian Doctors Validate CRIB-II Score as Key Predictor of Mortality in Premature Newborns
just_in.excerpt: A growing body of research from Indian hospitals confirms that the CRIB-II scoring system outperforms other tools in identifying premature neonates at highest risk of in-hospital death, with accuracy rates exceeding 88 percent.
just_in.image_caption: A medical professional caring for a newborn in a hospital setting. Recent Indian studies have validated the CRIB-II scoring system as a reliable predictor of mortality risk in premature neonates admitted to NICUs.
just_in.nri_angle: Indian-origin physicians and diaspora-led medical NGOs can use CRIB-II validation data to guide neonatal care investments and training programs in India.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: Lazy Aloo Toast: The 15-Minute Indian Snack Going Viral Online
just_in.excerpt: A stripped-down version of the classic Bombay aloo toast is sweeping social media feeds, requiring just boiled potatoes, bread, butter, and a handful of spices to produce a crispy, chaat-flavored snack in under 15 minutes.
just_in.image_caption: Slices of masala-topped bread toast arranged on a plate. The dish, rooted in Mumbai and Hyderabad street food traditions, has gained renewed attention through viral recipe shorts online.
just_in.image_credit: Photo by Muhammad Khawar Nazir on Pexels
just_in.nri_angle: The recipe uses pantry staples available at most Indian grocery stores and mainstream supermarkets in the US, UK, Canada, and Australia, making it an accessible way for the diaspora to recreate familiar street food flavors at home.

just_in.title: Your Thymus May Decide How Long You Live, Two Major Studies Find
just_in.excerpt: Harvard-led research published in Nature reveals the long-overlooked chest gland strongly predicts longevity, cardiovascular risk, and cancer immunotherapy outcomes in adults.
just_in.image_caption: A CT scanner of the kind used in the Harvard-led studies that analyzed thymic health in more than 27,000 adults. The research linked thymus condition to longevity and cancer immunotherapy outcomes.
just_in.nri_angle: Immunotherapy use is expanding rapidly across India's cancer centres and among diaspora patients; thymic health scores could eventually help clinicians personalise treatment for Indian-origin patients worldwide.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: DHS Ends Duration of Status for F-1 and J-1 Visas, Imposes Four-Year Cap
just_in.excerpt: The Department of Homeland Security has finalized a rule replacing the decades-old flexible visa system with fixed admission periods capped at four years, effective September 15. Universities and immigration experts are urging international students abroad to return to the U.S. before the deadline.
just_in.image_caption: International students on a university campus. The Trump administration's new rule ends the longstanding 'duration of status' framework for F-1 and J-1 visa holders, replacing it with fixed admission periods capped at four years.
just_in.nri_angle: India sends the largest number of international students to the U.S., with roughly 330,000 enrolled. The new four-year cap and stricter extension process will disproportionately affect Indian STEM graduate students. The MEA has said it is actively monitoring the situation.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: US Missile Stockpiles Hit Critical Lows as Iran War Drags On
just_in.excerpt: Analysts warn America has burned through up to 61% of its Patriot missiles and 80% of THAAD interceptors, raising questions about the Pentagon’s ability to sustain prolonged operations — and its readiness for threats elsewhere.
just_in.nri_angle: US munitions depletion could delay defense deliveries to India and push New Delhi to accelerate indigenous manufacturing under Atmanirbhar Bharat.

just_in.title: Disney's Moana Remake Earns $177 Million Worldwide but Braces for Major Loss
just_in.excerpt: The live-action Moana has crossed $177 million globally after two weekends, but with a $250 million production budget and steep drops, Deadline estimates Disney could lose $100–125 million on the film.
just_in.nri_angle: The original Moana became a cultural touchstone across South Asian and Pacific Islander communities; the remake's struggles raise questions about Disney's live-action strategy for future beloved animated properties.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: Judge Blocks Sony's Bid to Add 30,000 Songs to Udio AI Lawsuit
just_in.excerpt: A federal judge denied Sony Music's request to massively expand its copyright case against AI music generator Udio, keeping the suit limited to 333 works as the label stands alone among majors still litigating.
just_in.nri_angle: Indian music rights holders including T-Series and Saregama face similar questions about AI training on copyrighted works; the case could set global precedents for how AI companies use copyrighted recordings from regional markets.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: The Last Iron Lung Users Are Gone, but Polio Still Isn't
just_in.excerpt: With the deaths of Paul Alexander and Martha Lillard, the iron lung era has ended in the United States — yet experts warn that the virus remains a global threat, particularly as vaccine hesitancy grows.
just_in.image_caption: Paul Alexander in his iron lung in 1986. He contracted polio at age six in 1952 and spent the next 72 years in the device, becoming the Guinness World Record holder for longest time in an iron lung.
just_in.nri_angle: India eliminated polio in 2014 through a massive vaccination campaign — a public health triumph the diaspora can take pride in. But with wild poliovirus still circulating in neighboring Pakistan and vaccine hesitancy growing globally, the story remains unfinished.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: NSE Launches India’s First Ahimsa Index for Non-Violence-Based Investing
just_in.excerpt: The Nifty500 Ahimsa Index, developed with the Ahimsagain Foundation, screens 326 companies from India’s Nifty 500 by their alignment with non-violence principles, excluding firms tied to animal harm, alcohol, tobacco, and weapons.
just_in.image_caption: A stock market data screen displays live trading figures. NSE Indices has launched a new thematic benchmark that filters companies by their adherence to non-violence principles.
just_in.nri_angle: Jain and vegetarian diaspora communities gain a structured benchmark aligned with Ahimsa values; potential ETF/index fund products could give NRI investors ethical allocation options.

news.excerpt: The Family Grocery and Farmer Relief Act would force Tyson, JBS, Cargill, and National Beef to choose a single protein line, targeting an industry where four companies control 85% of U.S. beef processing.

news.excerpt: After social media backlash, the premier engineering institute clarified that an internal email asking students not to 'show affinity to political movements' was an annual advisory, not a new directive issued amid the ongoing CJP protests.
news.image_caption: A modern university building in Dehradun, Uttarakhand, near IIT Roorkee's campus. The institute faced backlash after issuing an advisory warning students against engaging with political movements.

news.title: Bengaluru Triple Murder Accused Used AI Chatbot for Six Months to Plan Killings
news.excerpt: Police say Kenneth, 25, consulted an AI chatbot about killing methods, body disposal, and evidence removal before the June stabbing of his partner's parents and sister. Investigators have now written to the AI company seeking his full chat history.
news.image_caption: A laptop displays an AI chatbot interface. Bengaluru police say the accused in a triple murder case used an AI chatbot for six months to plan the killings and research methods of evidence disposal.

news.title: Pentagon Faces Funding Crisis as Iran War Costs Spiral Beyond $29 Billion
news.excerpt: The Defense Department is burning through cash faster than expected, but key Republicans are balking at a $95 billion emergency spending package, demanding more transparency on war costs and strategy before signing off.
news.image_caption: The Pentagon, headquarters of the U.S. Department of Defense, in Arlington, Virginia. The building houses the sprawling bureaucracy now scrambling to secure tens of billions in emergency war funding from a skeptical Congress.

news.title: Two Indian Men Jailed in Singapore After Swapping $235,000 Diamond With Fake Stone at Chinatown Jeweller
news.excerpt: The pair posed as customers, replaced the diamond with a counterfeit during inspection, and were arrested at Changi Airport hours later while trying to flee the country.
news.image_caption: A diamond displayed in a jewellery store setting. Two Indian men were arrested in Singapore for swapping a S$235,000 diamond with a fake stone at a Chinatown shop.
news.nri_angle: The case is the latest in a series of theft arrests involving Indian nationals in Singapore, raising concerns about stereotyping within the Indian community abroad.

news.title: Lakhs March to Parliament Over NEET Paper Leak as Sonam Wangchuk's Hunger Strike Enters Day 23
news.excerpt: Tens of thousands of protesters clashed with police in New Delhi on the opening day of Parliament's monsoon session, demanding Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation over India's worst exam scandal in years.
news.image_caption: Sonam Wangchuk, the Ladakh-based activist whose 23-day hunger strike has become the focal point of India's anti-paper-leak movement. Wangchuk was forcibly moved to Safdarjung Hospital on July 18 after losing about 9 kg during his fast.
news.nri_angle: The crisis deepens skepticism among diaspora families about India's national testing infrastructure, especially those with children aspiring to medical seats back home.

news.title: Quad Unveils Fiji Port Project and Critical Minerals Pact at New Delhi Meeting
news.excerpt: Foreign ministers from India, the U.S., Japan, and Australia announced the Quad's first joint infrastructure project and new frameworks for critical minerals, energy security, and maritime surveillance at their May 26 meeting in New Delhi.
news.image_caption: India's External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar, who chaired the Quad Foreign Ministers' Meeting in New Delhi on May 26. The ministers announced the grouping's first joint infrastructure project in Fiji and new pacts on critical minerals and energy security.
news.nri_angle: The Quad's critical minerals framework and Pax Silica semiconductor initiative could accelerate foreign investment in India's technology manufacturing sector, creating new opportunities for Indian professionals in diversified global supply chains.

news.title: Sikkim Tunnel Death Toll Rises to Ten as Rescuers Battle Gas and Debris
news.excerpt: Ten bodies recovered from the collapsed ADIT-3 tunnel at NHPC's Teesta Stage VI hydroelectric project in Namchi district, with more than 15 workers still feared trapped inside the gas-filled passage.
news.image_caption: Police personnel at the site of the collapsed tunnel in Sikkim's Namchi district as rescue operations continue on Tuesday. At least ten workers have been killed and more than 15 remain trapped inside the NHPC hydroelectric project tunnel following a suspected gas explosion.
news.nri_angle: The victims hailed from migrant-worker communities in West Bengal, Assam, Punjab, and Uttarakhand, underscoring the human cost borne by India's mobile labour force in hazardous Himalayan construction.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Declares Indus Treaty 'Cannot Function,' Plans 5,500 MW of New J&K Hydro Projects
news.excerpt: New Delhi hardens its stance on the suspended water-sharing agreement with Pakistan, fast-tracking major dam projects on the Chenab and Jhelum rivers.
news.image_caption: The Baglihar Dam on the Chenab River in Jammu & Kashmir. India has fast-tracked several hydropower projects on the Chenab and Jhelum rivers after suspending the Indus Waters Treaty.
news.nri_angle: For diaspora members with roots in J&K, the hydropower push promises long-delayed economic development in a region historically constrained by treaty restrictions.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: One in 15 Million: Brisbane Mother Delivers Identical Quadruplets Sharing a Single Placenta
news.excerpt: Jenitar Na'amoana, 34, gave birth to four genetically identical girls at the Royal Brisbane and Women's Hospital in what doctors describe as an unprecedented monozygotic quadruplet pregnancy.
news.nri_angle: The birth has captured global attention as a rare medical milestone, resonating with families in the Indian and broader diaspora communities across Australia.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Congo Ebola Outbreak Hits 2,423 Cases and 967 Deaths as WHO Warns of Record Spread
news.excerpt: The Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak, now the third-largest Ebola outbreak ever recorded, continues to accelerate across five provinces with 80 percent of new cases emerging from unknown transmission chains.
news.nri_angle: The outbreak poses direct safety concerns for the Indian diaspora in East Africa and Indian health professionals working in the humanitarian response in DRC.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Ontario Wildfires Grow to 1.8 Million Acres as Smoke Chokes US Midwest
news.excerpt: Nearly 200 active blazes are burning across Ontario as wildfire smoke continues to trigger unhealthy air quality alerts across the US Midwest, stoking tensions between Washington and Ottawa.
news.image_caption: A forest fire burns through woodland terrain. Ontario wildfires have grown to 735,000 hectares as of July 20, with smoke drifting south into the US Midwest.
news.nri_angle: Large Indian diaspora populations in Toronto, Detroit, Chicago and other affected cities are directly impacted by the hazardous air quality from the wildfire smoke.

news.title: Seven Dead, Dozens Trapped as Landslide and Gas Leak Devastate Sikkim Tunnel
news.excerpt: A methane blast triggered a landslide that sealed an under-construction tunnel in Namchi district, trapping at least 27 workers as rescue teams battle toxic gas.
news.image_caption: Workers operate at a tunnel construction site on a mountain slope. The Sikkim tunnel collapse on Monday trapped at least 27 workers and killed seven, according to district officials.
news.nri_angle: The tragedy highlights ongoing infrastructure safety concerns in India's northeast, a region many NRIs trace their roots to.

news.title: 50,000 'Cockroach' Protesters March on Parliament as India's Monsoon Session Opens in Chaos
news.excerpt: Police fired tear gas and baton-charged demonstrators demanding the education minister's resignation over the NEET paper leak, as both houses of Parliament were adjourned amid the uproar.
news.image_caption: Activist Sonam Wangchuk, whose hospitalisation during a hunger strike galvanised Monday's massive protest. The 59-year-old is on his 23rd day of fasting in solidarity with the student-led movement.
news.nri_angle: The NEET paper leak directly affects students seeking to study medicine in India, including NRI families with children pursuing medical education through the Indian exam system.

news.excerpt: The second named storm of the 2026 Atlantic hurricane season is tracking toward the Florida Panhandle and Louisiana with storm surge watches and heavy rainfall warnings in effect.
news.nri_angle: Large Indian-American communities in Houston, the Florida Gulf Coast, and Louisiana should prepare for potential flooding and travel disruptions through the week.

news.excerpt: Douglas County reports a 'rapid' surge in cases tied to the fast-food chain, even as the FDA reverses its finding on Taylor Farms produce but maintains that fresh produce remains the primary suspected source.
news.image_caption: Fresh produce on display at a supermarket. The FDA continues to investigate fresh produce as the primary source of the record Cyclospora outbreak affecting over 6,700 people across the United States.

nri-world.excerpt: A Division Bench overturned a single-judge order that had refused the climate activist's transfer from Safdarjung Hospital, with government raising no objection to the move.
nri-world.image_caption: Sonam Wangchuk, the Ladakhi climate activist and education reformer, in a 2017 photograph. The Delhi High Court on Tuesday ordered his transfer from Safdarjung Hospital to Medanta Hospital after a legal battle over his medical care during a 24-day hunger strike.
nri-world.nri_angle: Wangchuk is internationally recognized for his ice stupa innovation and as the inspiration behind the Bollywood film 3 Idiots; his fast has drawn global attention to India's exam-reform movement.

nri-world.title: Miami's Cost of Living Surpasses New York City's for the First Time
nri-world.excerpt: Federal data shows the Miami metro area is now America's second most expensive region after San Francisco, as soaring insurance premiums, property taxes, and post-pandemic inflation erode Florida's no-income-tax advantage.
nri-world.image_caption: The Miami skyline rises above lush green parks under clear blue skies. The metro area has overtaken New York City as the second most expensive region in the United States, according to new federal data.
nri-world.nri_angle: Indian American professionals who relocated to South Florida during the pandemic for tax savings now face an all-in cost of living that may erode those benefits.

nri-world.title: Indian Diaspora Protests Outside India House in London Over NEET Controversy and Delhi Crackdown
nri-world.excerpt: Demonstrators demanded Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation over the NEET examination scandal and voiced solidarity with climate activist Sonam Wangchuk.
nri-world.image_caption: Protesters gathered outside a government building. Indian diaspora members demonstrated outside India House in London over the NEET exam controversy.
nri-world.nri_angle: Indian diaspora in the UK directly involved in political protest over domestic Indian issues, reflecting a growing trend of transnational activism.

nri-world.title: Mamata Rallies INDIA Bloc for Unity as TMC Split Deepens Ahead of Monsoon Session
nri-world.excerpt: Despite losing 20 MPs to a rebel faction and three Rajya Sabha members to the BJP, Mamata Banerjee is pushing opposition parties to close ranks against the ruling alliance as Parliament's monsoon session begins.
nri-world.image_caption: Mamata Banerjee, founder-chairperson of the Trinamool Congress, photographed in Kolkata. Banerjee is pushing for opposition unity through the INDIA bloc even as her party faces its deepest internal crisis since 1998.
nri-world.nri_angle: The TMC split and opposition realignment hold political and cultural significance for West Bengal's large diaspora community, shaping conversations about governance and democratic accountability in India.

nri-world.title: India Wins Two Golds and Four Silvers at International Mathematical Olympiad, Finishes Seventh Globally
nri-world.excerpt: A six-member Indian team delivered the country's fourth consecutive top-10 finish at the world's most prestigious maths competition, held in Shanghai with a record 680 participants from 117 nations.

nri-world.title: Satchin Panda Resigns From Salk Institute After Sexual Misconduct Allegations

nri-world.title: Punjab Farmers March on Delhi for Mahapanchayat Against US Trade Deal, Warning of Agricultural 'Devastation'

nri-world.title: Singapore’s Malayalee Community Kicks Off Three-Month Onam Season With Boat Race and Cultural Programme
nri-world.excerpt: From snake boat races at Jurong Lake to an Esplanade concert and a centenary celebration, Singapore’s Onam calendar features over a dozen events spanning July to October.
